claim: C3 (chromium-hscroll-domain-linux): primary-source grounding for the scrollend event and the horizontal scroll clamp

entries.claim: C3-scrollend-trigger-1: scrollend depends on the scroll being completed; a scroll is completed when the scroll position has no pending updates or translations and the user finished the gesture
entries.quote: when the scroll position has no more pending updates or translations and the user has completed their gesture.
entries.plainText: Scroll is completed when the scroll position has no more pending updates or translations and the user has completed their gesture.

entries.claim: C3-scrollend-fired-2: normative event-summary statement of when the scrollend event is fired (Document/element/VisualViewport, scroll sequence ended, offsets applied)
entries.quote: or element has been scrolled, the scroll sequence has ended and any scroll offset changes have
entries.plainText: Fired at the VisualViewport, Document, or element when a scroll is completed: the VisualViewport, viewport, or element has been scrolled, the scroll sequence has ended and any scroll offset changes have been applied.

entries.claim: C3-scrollend-absent-3: no scrollend event fires when the scroll position did not change (explains the boundary leg: a wheel at the clamp moves nothing, so no scrollend)
entries.quote: event fires because no scrolling occurred.
entries.plainText: If the scroll position did not change as a result of the user interaction or programmatic invocation, where no translations were applied as a result, then no scrollend event fires because no scrolling occurred.
entries.section: 3.1. Scrolling (note inside 'perform a scroll of a viewport')

entries.claim: C3-scrollend-dispatch-4: the scrollend event is queued as a pending scroll event on the target and later fired
entries.plainText: Append (target, "scrollend") to doc's pending scroll events.

entries.claim: C3-viewport-hscroll-clamp-5: the Window/Viewport horizontal scroll position is clamped to viewport scrolling area width minus viewport width (the bound the C3 fixture hits)
entries.quote: Let x be max(0, min(x, viewport scrolling area width - viewport width)).
entries.plainText: Let x be max(0, min(x, viewport scrolling area width - viewport width)).
entries.section: 4. Extensions to the Window Interface (window scroll algorithm)

entries.claim: C3-element-hscroll-clamp-6: the Element horizontal scroll position is clamped to element scrolling area width minus element padding edge width
entries.quote: Let x be max(0, min(x, element scrolling area width - element padding edge width)).
entries.plainText: Let x be max(0, min(x, element scrolling area width - element padding edge width)).

entries.claim: C3-scrollleft-setter-7: setting scrollLeft runs the setter steps, which end in 'scroll an element' (i.e. the clamp above)
entries.quote: When setting the scrollLeft attribute these steps must be run:
entries.plainText: When setting the scrollLeft attribute these steps must be run:

entries.claim: C3-scrollable-overflow-bound-8: the scrollable overflow (the bound used by the clamp) is the set of things extending outside the box's padding edge
entries.quote: set of things extending outside of that box’s padding edge
entries.plainText: The scrollable overflow of a box is the set of things extending outside of that box's padding edge for which a scrolling mechanism needs to be provided.

reproduce: For each entry: cd <seat dir> && grep -n -F '<quote>' <stagedFile>  -> the recorded line, exactly one hit.
notes: The C3 fixture scrolls the top-level document (window.scrollX), so entry 5 (viewport clamp) is the bound that applies; entry 6 is the Element-level analogue.

Driver facts (frozen driver scripts/chrome-cdp-loopback-round67.mjs, sha256 ac0561ac85fb4ce544e728d6805da1e477a45e23cdd66d0e9573e103130a70e0): VIEWPORT = { width: 1280, height: 900 } (line 48), CONTENT_WIDTH = 2280. Entry 5 gives max scrollLeft = 2280 - 1280 = 1000, which equals the MEASURED clamp (scrollLeft 1000 on the overscroll and boundary legs) and matches the L1's REFUTED smoke1 note that 2240px content would have given 960.
Entry 3 is the primary-source basis for the boundary leg firing NO scrollend: at the clamp the scroll position does not change, so no scrolling occurred.
